title: San Diego State shocks No. 15 Boise State 22-20 with game-winning field goal
summary: Cooper DiLeva kicked a 42-yard field goal as time expired as San Diego State scored nine points in the last two minutes to shock No. 15 Boise State 22-20 on Saturday night.
text:
BOISE, Idaho (AP) — Cooper DiLeva kicked a 42-yard field goal as time expired as San Diego State scored nine points in the last two minutes to shock No. 15 Boise State 22-20 on Saturday night.
Boise State (9-2, 6-1 Pac-12; No. 17 CFP) watched its playoff hopes take a big hit as the Broncos squandered a late 20-13 lead.
San Diego State (6-5, 5-2) clinched a spot in the Pac-12 championship game and will return to Boise for a rematch on Dec. 4.
“We knew it was going to be a 60-minute fight, and we used every single second of what it was, to find a way to win,” San Diego State coach Sean Lewis said. “Even better, we have punched our ticket to come back here in two weeks and partake in the first Pac-12 championship against a really good team.”
Despite some early struggles, Boise State seemed poised to escape with a victory before the Aztecs rallied.
But a spectacular 37-yard touchdown catch by Jaylon Hawkins, in which he wrestled the ball away in the end zone from an apparent interception by Sherrod Smith, pulled San Diego State within 20-19 with 1:51 to play.
San Diego State failed on a 2-point conversion attempt and the Broncos recovered an onside kick, but couldn’t get a first down to salt away the game.
Instead of punting on fourth-and-3 at the Aztecs 45, Boise State coach Spencer Danielson went for the first down, but quarterback Maddux Madsen was dragged down for a 1-yard loss. The Broncos had converted 13 straight fourth-down plays before coming up short.
“We’re going to be aggressive and that’s our mentality,” Danielson said. “It’s fourth-and-3 for the game. Looking at it after the fact, it didn’t go our way. But if you get it, the game’s over. We didn’t get it done in the moment, and that’s on me.”
Stone Saunders, who threw for 227 yards and rushed for 41 more, only needed two completions of seven and 24 yards to set up DiLeva for the winning kick.

“Coop’s the guy,” Saunders said of his kicker. “He’s got ice in his veins, and we know that, especially on the last drive. Just get close and give him a chance.”
Madsen threw for 311 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions.
The takeaway
Boise State: After averaging more than 50 points in their last three games, the Broncos leaned on defense, which couldn’t deliver in the game’s biggest moments. The Boise State defense has been pushed to the brink in several games, and it finally cost them — not only the game but also possibly a playoff berth.
San Diego State: The Aztecs have played better defensively since melting down last month in a 56-49 loss to Colorado State. Now they have a chance to secure their first Pac-12 conference title in two weeks.

text:
Idaho nonprofit Envision provides the gift of sight and hearing
Envision offers free vision clinics for those at, or below, the poverty levels, and demand is high, writes guest columnist Chuck Malloy.
Idaho nonprofit Envision helps provide eye exams, eyeglasses and frames for free or at discounted rates, depending on income levels. (Photo by Getty Images)
Jay Lugo, the executive director of Envision, figures he’s had a good day if his nonprofit enterprise can help one person with vision or hearing loss.
Lugo has had a lot of good days during his 32 years leading the Lions Clubs-affiliated nonprofit, and he has seen thousands of Idahoans helped along the way.
“I’ve seen people break down and cry when they put on a pair of glasses and discover they are able to see,” Lugo says. “It fills my heart with joy being able to do that – and I sleep well at night knowing that we are making a difference. But it’s not just me. It’s the volunteers and office co-workers who see that happen, and the 1,400 Lions Club members throughout the state who get information about what’s being done. So, a lot of people are involved.”
And Lance Grady of Boise is glad for that. He didn’t break down in tears when he recently was fitted with glasses, but he did look across a street and see a squirrel climbing a tree. And he could see letters, numbers and names on buildings.
“I wouldn’t have been able to see any of that without my glasses,” he said. “This has been life changing. I can drive and do other things that I was unable to do.”
Grady’s story began by word of mouth.
“A family friend talked with me about reaching out to the Lions,” he said. “They were determined to help me find something – without spending $400 for a pair of glasses. “I’m so thankful … a lot of stress has been lifted from me.”
Lugo has seen similar stories play out many times.
“When people are able to see, they can get a driver’s license, fill out a job application and be productive,” Lugo says. “There is such a big gap with healthcare, and we’re only talking about eyesight and hearing. The state doesn’t provide aid with eyeglasses for those over the age of 18, so you are not going to get eyecare assistance if you are at the poverty level.”
Envision helps fill the void, providing exams, eyeglasses and frames for free or at discounted rates, depending on income levels. Envision offers free vision clinics for those at, or below, the poverty levels, and Lugo says demand is high.
“I get at least 20 applications in my email box every day, which is about 600 a month,” he says. “Every one of those are from people who need glasses and are at the poverty level. There are a lot of people who are hurting.”
Envision started in 1969 as Idaho’s only eye bank and arranging corneal transplants remain a big part of the nonprofit’s operation – along with the tradition of collecting and refurbishing used eyeglasses. title: More showers and cooler weather sticking around Idaho
summary: Another round of rain and snow is coming in for Idaho. Cooler weather will stick around, but temperatures will warm slightly.
text:
Another round of rain and snow is coming in for Idaho. Cooler weather will stick around, but temperatures will warm slightly.
What an amazing winter-like week for Idaho ski resorts. Over two feet of snow at Bogus Basin, 30" inches up at Tamarack, and Sun Valley saw 15" over the last week. Compared to this time last year, it's a breath of fresh air, and more is set to come.
Saturday saw a decent break from precipitation, but Sunday morning is set to see another round pass over Oregon and into the Gem State. Regions like Twin Falls should stay dry, but the Treasure Valley and central mountains will see some activity to close out the weekend.
A nice forecast after that with clearer weather on the way. Temperatures for the valley floors will be into the 40s and by next weekend climb back into he 50s. There are chances of showers on Thursday, and we will key in on those once we get closer to the day.
Extended outlooks are tracking warmer than normal but not like what we experienced last year. The better news is more showers are on the way heading into December. If you're not a fan of rain, I am sorry, but when it comes to southern Idaho's drought conditions that have carried over from last year, we need as much rain and snow as we can get.
It is also beautiful seeing our mountains dusted with a layer of snow, so enjoy the nice view and have a wonderful weekend!
